conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed for the Hilbert adjoint and compact spectral decomposition; no full Choice or basis of the kernel is selected.
λ is the coefficient of the squared penalty, so Hansen's λ_H satisfies λ=λ_H². Source order ν refers to (A*A)^ν, corresponding to Clason's |A| exponent 2ν.

Spectral sums are norm limits of finite-subset nets over nonzero eigenspaces, with the kernel component treated separately. Positive powers vanish on the kernel; qualification is vacuous when there are no nonzero eigenvalues.

GCV replaces diagonal leverages by their trace average in the mean leave-one-out squared error. Equality as functions of all data holds exactly when all diagonal leverages agree; equality for one datum can be accidental.
Finite-grid GCV minimizes only its supplied score and resolves ties by the smallest index.

The L-curve rule discards zero residuals or solution norms, assigns unsigned three-point curvature to interior retained indices, sets degenerate curvature to zero, and resolves maximum ties by the least original index.

Morozov uses exact residual evaluation and supplied exact range-distance and data-norm endpoints. Compatibility is the strict inequality d<τδ<G; finite budget exhaustion is inconclusive, and success returns a bracket.
The discretized datum is A_h x†+e before inversion. Forward-model error, regularized-operator difference, exact normal residual, and certified residual-evaluation error remain separate contributions.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For a compact self-adjoint operator on a real or complex Hilbert space, every bounded scalar multiplier on {0} together with its nonzero eigenvalues defines a norm-convergent finite-subset spectral sum and a bounded linear operator of norm at most the supremum of the multiplier's absolute value.

Assume Countable Choice. Let X,Y be real or complex Hilbert spaces and let A:X→Y be compact and bounded, with adjoint A*. Then both A*A and AA* are compact, self-adjoint and positive, and ker(A*A)=ker A, ker(AA*)=ker A*.

For compact A between real or complex Hilbert spaces under Countable Choice, S=A*A has spectral multipliers; S^ν uses t^ν on positive eigenspaces and zero on the kernel. Tikhonov uses g_λ(t)=1/(t+λ), r_λ(t)=λ/(t+λ), and x_λ^δ=(A*A+λI)⁻¹A*y_δ. Qualification at least p requires t^ν|r_α(t)|≤C_ν α^ν for every α>0, t∈Σ, and 0<ν≤p.

Assume Countable Choice and compact A between real or complex Hilbert spaces. For g∈Y, r_g(λ)=||A(A*A+λI)⁻¹A*g−g|| is continuous and nondecreasing on (0,∞), with limits dist(g,closure(Ran A)) at zero and ||g|| at infinity. Its residual vector is λ(AA*+λI)⁻¹g, and the residual operator has norm at most one.

Assume Countable Choice. For compact A between real or complex Hilbert spaces, x†⊥ker A and y=Ax†, the exact-data bias is the spectral sum of λ/(t+λ)P_t x† and tends to zero in norm as λ decreases to zero.
Assume Countable Choice. For compact A between real or complex Hilbert spaces, S=A*A, x†=S^νw, 0<ν≤1 and ||w||≤R, the exact-data Tikhonov bias is at most Rλ^ν for every λ>0.

For real A∈R^(m×n), m≥1, b∈R^m and λ>0, the deleted-observation residual equals ((I−H_λ)b)_i/(1−(H_λ)_ii), with positive denominator. Replacing the leverages by their average in the mean squared deleted residual gives ||(I−H_λ)b||²/[m(1−tr(H_λ)/m)²].
The real sequence space ℓ²(N,R), with its canonical inner product and norm, is complete and therefore is a real Hilbert space.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit choice assumption for Hilbert adjoints, orthogonal decomposition and compact spectral results.
Adjoint existence under Countable Choice and the linear-first adjoint identity.
Self-adjointness and positivity of the Gram operators.
Domains and boundedness hypotheses for operator compositions and shifted normal inverses.
Compactness conventions and compact operators being bounded.
Linear-first convention, conjugate symmetry and positive definiteness.
Norm-square identities and triangle inequalities.
Composition reversal, double adjoints and operator-norm identities.
Compactness of A*A and AA*.
Real nonzero eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenspaces, kernel decomposition and norm-convergent spectral sums.
Cauchy-sequence completeness and real/complex Hilbert-space conventions.
Minimum-norm solution hypotheses and range/kernel orthogonality.
Kernel and closed-range orthogonal projections under Countable Choice.
Unit-ball norm bounds, including zero spaces, and the forward perturbation estimate.
Finite-subsum definitions, small tails and the canonical ℓ² inner product.
Existence of the finite supremum of a bounded multiplier.
Coordinate limits in the local ℓ² completeness proof.
The finite-dimensional objective and squared-penalty coefficient convention.
Unique finite-matrix Tikhonov solutions, including row-deleted GCV problems.
Hat-matrix eigenvalues and positivity of GCV denominators.
Compactness of coordinate truncations in the diagonal examples and saturation witness.
Compactness of the diagonal operators from explicit norm-convergent truncations.
Existence of exact Morozov roots and roots inside successful brackets.

concerns.concern: The Definition begins 'Input a compact operator A:X→Y between real or complex Hilbert spaces' without explicitly assuming Countable Choice. Its adjoint and shifted-inverse suppliers require that assumption, and the accompanying convergence theorem states it explicitly. The intended setting is recoverable from the dependencies, but the procedure's admissible setting should state the same assumption.

seams_checked.note: Checked the shifted-normal inverse lemma, noise-amplification lemma and full error-chain theorem against their actual uses. The 1/λ and 1/(2√λ) bounds retain their Hilbert-space and Countable Choice hypotheses. The forward-discretization theorem preserves the five-term identity and separately assumes decay of the regularized-operator difference; it imports no automatic perturbation or arithmetic certificate. The algorithm's omitted explicit choice assumption is recorded as a presentation concern.

Checked the Landweber filter identities, source/noise theorem and discrepancy-rate corollary. They use the Gram positivity/kernel result, spectral multiplier bound and source-power convention with explicit Countable Choice. Polynomial filters retain their kernel values, exact-data convergence assumes x†⊥ker A, and source estimates use the same powers of A*A. No Tikhonov qualification limitation is incorrectly transferred to Landweber.
